content: 1. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of propranolol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Ritonavir significantly increases the levels or effects of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Quercetin decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs may increase each other's toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Avoid co-administration with drugs that prolong QT intervals or in patients with risk factors for QT prolongation. Monitor closely. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Quinidine also increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quinupristin/dalfopristin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Reduce quizartinib dosage when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 9. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 10. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 11. Ranolazine increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Ritonavir also increases ranolazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is chemically identical to lovastatin, increasing the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Ritonavir increases regorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to increased toxicity and reduced exposure to active metabolites M-2 and M-5. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid co-administration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 17. Ritonavir increases the levels of revefenacin by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters, leading to increased systemic exposure to its active metabolite. Co-administration is not recommended. 18. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. 19. Ritonavir increases rifabutin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rifabutin decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Rifampin decreases ritonavir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Rifapentine decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 22. Ritonavir increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ritonavir increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine increases ritonavir toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Ritonavir increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Ritonavir increases riociguat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and adjust the dose if necessary. 26. Ritonavir increases ripretinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing systemic exposure to its active metabolite DP-5439. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Ritonavir increases risperidone levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 28. Ritonavir increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration due to increased bleeding risk. 29. Ritonavir decreases roflumilast levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Ritonavir increases roflumilast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Ritonavir increases rosuvastatin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, increasing the risk of myopathy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Ritonavir increases rucaparib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 33. Ritonavir decreases rufinamide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Ritonavir increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 35. Ritonavir increases sacubitril/valsartan levels by decreasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Ritonavir increases salmeterol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to increased toxicity. 37. Sarecycline increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor for toxicities. 38. Ritonavir increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 39. Ritonavir increases seladelpar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers. 40. Ritonavir increases selexipag levels by inhibiting metabolism. This interaction is likely of little clinical significance. 41. Ritonavir increases selpercatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Ritonavir increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage. 43. Ritonavir increases sertraline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Ritonavir increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If used for erectile dysfunction, limit sildenafil to 25 mg within 48 hours. Sildenafil for pulmonary arterial hypertension is not recommended with ritonavir. 45. Ritonavir increases silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. This combination is contraindicated. 46. Ritonavir increases simvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. This combination is contraindicated due to increased risk of myopathy. 47. Ritonavir increases siponimod levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
